lines.trans: Still raining outside, Mateo. Will green paint dry indoors before Wednesday?
It will if we lay brown paper here and move warm air down the hallway.
It is water-based garden paint: low smell and fast drying if the air keeps moving.

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)

lines.trans: Where do we point the small fan, Javier?
Crack the courtyard transom two centimetres and blow the dry air toward it.
Smart! Dry air flows past the wood without letting a single drop of rain in.
Look at the colour in the tin when I stir it: deep linden-leaf green!
Thin strokes along the grain, Clara. Thick paint stays sticky.
First coat before lunch, second tonight, and hard as stone tomorrow afternoon!
Hand me the wide brush, Mateo: shutter number one is mine!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: Save a thin brush for the corners... and watch the door in case Ernesto walks by.

words.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

lines.trans: Too late: here comes Ernesto in his clean white Monday shirt!

words.gloss: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.

examples.text: Ayer abrimos la tienda temprano.
examples.trans: Yesterday we opened the shop early.

meanings.note: Feminine noun that takes el in the singular before stressed initial /a/ (el agua fría).

examples.text: Quiero un vaso de agua fría.
examples.trans: I want a glass of cold water.

examples.text: El agua de la ducha sale caliente.
examples.trans: The shower water comes out hot.

meanings.note: Points to something at medium distance or near the listener.

examples.text: Deja las llaves ahí en la mesa.
examples.trans: Leave the keys there on the table.

examples.text: Ahí viene el autobús.
examples.trans: There comes the bus.

meanings.note: Al aire libre means 'outdoors'.

examples.text: Abre la ventana, necesitamos aire fresco.
examples.trans: Open the window, we need fresh air.

examples.text: El aire del mar es muy limpio.
examples.trans: The sea air is very clean.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Points to a place farther away from both speakers.

examples.text: La farmacia está allí en la esquina.
examples.trans: The pharmacy is over there on the corner.

examples.text: Vivimos allí durante seis años.
examples.trans: We lived there for six years.

meanings.note: Opposite of estrecho (narrow).

examples.text: La calle es ancha y tranquila.
examples.trans: The street is wide and quiet.

examples.text: La cama mide un metro y medio de ancho.
examples.trans: The bed is a metre and a half wide.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.text: Llegué diez minutos antes.
examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Everyday word in Spain for writing down a note or phone number.

examples.text: Apunto la dirección en un papel.
examples.trans: I jot down the address on a piece of paper.

examples.text: ¿Apuntaste el nombre del cliente?
examples.trans: Did you write down the guest's name?

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.text: Todo va muy bien hoy.
examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.

examples.text: El té sale bien caliente.
examples.trans: The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Quedarse blanco means 'to go pale'.

examples.text: Quiero una camisa blanca.
examples.trans: I want a white shirt.

examples.text: Las paredes del baño son blancas.
examples.trans: The bathroom walls are white.

meanings.note: A container for paint, jam, coins or pens.

examples.text: Hay un bote de mermelada en la mesa.
examples.trans: There is a jar of jam on the table.

examples.text: Compramos dos botes de pintura blanca.
examples.trans: We buy two tins of white paint.

meanings.note: Brocha is a wide decorator's/carpenter's brush, whereas pincel is narrower.

examples.text: Lava las brochas con agua templada al terminar.
examples.trans: Wash the paintbrushes with warm water when you finish.

examples.text: Escurre bien la brocha en el borde del bote.
examples.trans: Wipe the brush well on the rim of the tin.

meanings.note: Formed from brocha + -azo ('stroke with a brush').

examples.text: Da brochazos largos y suaves de arriba abajo.
examples.trans: Use long, gentle brushstrokes from top to bottom.

examples.text: Con dos brochazos más cubrimos toda la esquina.
examples.trans: With two more brushstrokes we cover the whole corner.

meanings.note: Buttoned shirt.

examples.text: La camisa está aquí.
examples.trans: The shirt is here.

examples.text: Vemos las camisas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shirts from the door.

meanings.note: Una capa de pintura means 'a coat of paint'.

examples.text: Mañana daremos la segunda capa de verde a las lamas.
examples.trans: Tomorrow we will give the slats their second coat of green.

examples.text: Extiende una capa fina de crema sobre la base.
examples.trans: Spread a thin layer of curd over the crust.

meanings.note: Proparoxytone; keeps the written accent on -tí- in the plural centímetros.

examples.text: Faltan tres centímetros para llegar al marco de piedra.
examples.trans: It is three centimetres short of reaching the stone frame.

examples.text: Corta la masa en tiras iguales de dos centímetros.
examples.trans: Cut the dough into even two-centimetre strips.

meanings.note: Masculine in standard Spanish: el color / los colores.

examples.text: Ese color verde queda precioso junto a la cal blanca.
examples.trans: That green colour looks lovely beside the whitewash.

examples.text: A plena luz del sol se ven mejor los colores.
examples.trans: In full sunlight you can see the colours better.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Comemos juntos a las dos de la tarde.
examples.trans: We have lunch together at two in the afternoon.

examples.text: Comí un trozo de bizcocho de limón.
examples.trans: I ate a piece of lemon sponge cake.

meanings.note: Unaccented como compares or gives a reason (distinct from interrogative cómo).

examples.text: Está fría como el agua del río.
examples.trans: It is as cold as river water.

examples.text: Todo funciona como debe ser.
examples.trans: Everything works just as it should.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Wooden outer or inner shutter hinged beside a window.

examples.text: Cierra las contraventanas por la noche.
examples.trans: Close the shutters at night.

examples.text: Las contraventanas de madera son verdes.
examples.trans: The wooden shutters are green.

meanings.note: Entrar/salir corriendo = to run in / run out.

examples.text: Corro para no perder el tren.
examples.trans: I run so I do not miss the train.

examples.text: Los niños corrieron hacia la fuente.
examples.trans: The children ran toward the fountain.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

demasiado.gloss: too much; too many; too (as adv)

meanings.en: too much; too many; too (as adv)
meanings.note: Agrees as a determiner before a noun (demasiado tiempo); invariable as an adverb before an adjective.

examples.text: Tres años era demasiado tiempo.
examples.trans: Three years was too much time.

examples.text: No camines demasiado rápido.
examples.trans: Do not walk too fast.

meanings.note: Dentro de + time means 'in (after) a certain amount of time'.

examples.text: Hay cuatro mesas dentro.
examples.trans: There are four tables inside.

examples.text: Vuelvo dentro de diez minutos.
examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Hacerse el duro = to act tough.

examples.text: Es una pieza dura.
examples.trans: It is a hard piece.

examples.text: se hacía el duro
examples.trans: acted tough

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.text: Mira dónde señala con el lápiz.
examples.trans: Look where he is pointing with his pencil.

examples.text: ¿Dónde van las cucharillas y las servilletas?
examples.trans: Where do the teaspoons and the napkins go?

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Seen on shop doors opposite tirar (pull).

examples.text: Empuja la puerta de madera suavemente.
examples.trans: Push the wooden door gently.

examples.text: Empujamos la mesa hacia la sombra.
examples.trans: We pushed the table into the shade.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

entrar.gloss: to come in; to go in; to enter

meanings.en: to come in; to go in; to enter
meanings.note: Pairs with en in Spain (entrar en la posada).

examples.text: Entra mucha luz por el balcón.
examples.trans: Plenty of light comes in through the balcony.

examples.text: Entramos en la tienda para resguardarnos.
examples.trans: We stepped into the shop to shelter.

esquina.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

meanings.en: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)
meanings.note: Outer corner where two streets meet, or the crisp corner of a baking tray.

examples.text: La esquina está aquí.
examples.trans: The corner is here.

examples.text: Vemos las esquinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the corners from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.text: Este patio es muy tranquilo.
examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.

examples.text: Esta mañana hace mucho sol.
examples.trans: This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Describes thin glass/fabric as well as fine quality.

examples.text: El cristal de estos vasos es demasiado fino para el té.
examples.trans: The glass of these cups is too thin for tea.

examples.text: Corta el limón en rodajas muy finas.
examples.trans: Cut the lemon into very thin slices.

meanings.note: Por fuera = on the outside.

examples.text: Hace frío fuera esta mañana.
examples.trans: It is cold outside this morning.

examples.text: La maleta es azul por fuera.
examples.trans: The suitcase is blue on the outside.

meanings.note: Ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: Cae una gota de lluvia en mi mano.
examples.trans: A drop of rain falls on my hand.

examples.text: Solo quiero unas gotas de leche.
examples.trans: I only want a few drops of milk.

meanings.note: Describes thick envelopes, walls, or coats.

examples.text: Necesito un abrigo grueso para el invierno.
examples.trans: I need a thick coat for winter.

examples.text: Este libro es muy grueso.
examples.trans: This book is very thick.

guardar.gloss: to keep; to put away; to guard

meanings.en: to keep; to put away; to guard
meanings.note: Everyday verb for putting something safely away in a pocket or cupboard.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en este cajón.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in this drawer.

examples.text: Te guardé el último rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I saved the last cinnamon roll for you.

meanings.note: Indicates direction of movement or gaze.

examples.text: Camina hacia el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: Walk toward the stone bridge.

examples.text: Sigue mirando hacia la esquina.
examples.trans: Keep looking toward the corner.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Means both a tree leaf and a single sheet of paper.

examples.text: La hoja está aquí.
examples.trans: The leaf is here.

examples.text: Vemos las hojas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the leaves from the door.

meanings.note: Plural jardines, without the written accent.

examples.text: Mi madre tiene flores en el jardín.
examples.trans: My mother has flowers in the garden.

examples.text: Los niños juegan en el jardín.
examples.trans: The children play in the garden.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.text: La habitación ya está limpia.
examples.trans: The room is already clean.

examples.text: Necesito una toalla limpia.
examples.trans: I need a clean towel.

meanings.note: Impersonal stem-changing verb (o -> ue: llueve).

examples.text: Hoy llueve mucho en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is raining heavily in Valencia.

examples.text: Anoche llovió hasta las diez.
examples.trans: Last night it rained until ten.

meanings.note: Bajo la lluvia = in the rain.

examples.text: La lluvia es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The rain is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la lluvia.
examples.trans: We talk about the rain.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.

examples.text: ¡Hasta luego, que tengas buen día!
examples.trans: See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el lunes, los lunes.

examples.text: El lunes está aquí.
examples.trans: The Monday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lunes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Mondays from the door.

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.text: La mesa es de madera.
examples.trans: The table is made of wood.

examples.text: Me gusta el olor de la madera.
examples.trans: I like the smell of wood.

meanings.note: Plural marrones.

examples.text: Es una pieza marrón.
examples.trans: It is a brown piece.

examples.text: Dos pares de zapatos marrones de hombre y jerséis grises.
examples.trans: Two pairs of men's brown shoes and grey sweaters.

meanings.note: La mañana = the morning; mañana (without article) = tomorrow.

examples.text: Por la mañana servimos café caliente.
examples.trans: In the morning we serve hot coffee.

examples.text: ¡Hasta mañana a las ocho!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow at eight!

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el miércoles, los miércoles.

examples.text: El miércoles está aquí.
examples.trans: The Wednesday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los miércoles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Wednesdays from the door.

meanings.note: Small hinged window pane set above a door to let air circulate.

examples.text: Abre un poco el montante alto para ventilar el pasillo.
examples.trans: Open the high transom window slightly to air the hallway.

examples.text: La luz de la mañana entra por el montante de cristal.
examples.trans: Morning light comes in through the glass fanlight.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: muevo).

examples.text: Movemos la mesa bajo la sombra.
examples.trans: We move the table into the shade.

examples.text: El viento suave movió las hojas.
examples.trans: The gentle breeze stirred the leaves.

meanings.note: Stressed possessive (el mío, la mía, los míos, las mías); ¡Madre mía! = Goodness me!

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

examples.text: Un amigo mío vive en esta calle.
examples.trans: A friend of mine lives on this street.

meanings.note: Ni... ni... = neither... nor...; ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: No cae ni una sola gota.
examples.trans: Not a single drop is falling.

examples.text: No tengo ni papel ni bolígrafo.
examples.trans: I have neither paper nor pen.

meanings.note: ¡Buenas noches! = Good evening / Good night; esta noche = tonight.

examples.text: La noche está aquí.
examples.trans: The night is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the nights from the door.

oler.gloss: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)

meanings.en: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)
meanings.note: Irregular boot stem hue- (huelo, hueles, huele, huelen).

examples.text: La cocina huele a canela caliente.
examples.trans: The kitchen smells like warm cinnamon.

examples.text: El jardín huele a flores frescas.
examples.trans: The garden smells of fresh flowers.

meanings.note: Azul oscuro = dark blue; gris oscuro = dark grey.

examples.text: El pasillo está muy oscuro.
examples.trans: The hallway is very dark.

examples.text: Prefiero el chocolate oscuro.
examples.trans: I prefer dark chocolate.

meanings.note: Plural los papeles.

examples.text: Necesito papel y un bolígrafo.
examples.trans: I need paper and a pen.

examples.text: Escribe tu nombre en este papel.
examples.trans: Write your name on this piece of paper.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.text: ¡Pase, por favor, y siéntese!
examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

meanings.note: The corridor inside a house, hotel or train.

examples.text: El baño está al final del pasillo.
examples.trans: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.

examples.text: No corras por el pasillo.
examples.trans: Don't run in the corridor.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.text: Los niños juegan en el patio.
examples.trans: The children play in the courtyard.

examples.text: Desayunamos en el patio cuando hace sol.
examples.trans: We have breakfast in the courtyard when it's sunny.

meanings.note: From pegar ('to stick'); used for wet paint, syrup, or humid heat.

examples.text: No toques el marco aún: el barniz sigue pegajoso.
examples.trans: Do not touch the frame yet: the varnish is still tacky.

examples.text: Lávate las manos si te quedan pegajosas de limón.
examples.trans: Wash your hands if they feel sticky with lemon.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from pensar.

examples.text: Es una pieza pensada.
examples.trans: It is a thought-out piece.

examples.text: Bien pensado, Clara. Javier lee normas municipales de edificios cada semana.
examples.trans: Smart thinking, Clara. Javier reads city building rules every single week.

meanings.note: Hermano pequeño = younger brother; de pequeño = as a child.

examples.text: Tengo un piso pequeño.
examples.trans: I have a small flat.

examples.text: Mi hermana pequeña tiene diez años.
examples.trans: My little sister is ten.

meanings.note: De piedra = made of stone.

examples.text: La casa tiene paredes de piedra.
examples.trans: The house has stone walls.

examples.text: Hay una piedra en mi zapato.
examples.trans: There's a stone in my shoe.

meanings.note: Pintura fresca = wet paint.

examples.text: Necesitamos pintura blanca para el baño.
examples.trans: We need white paint for the bathroom.

examples.text: Me encanta la pintura española.
examples.trans: I love Spanish painting.

meanings.note: Un poco de mantequilla = a little butter.

examples.text: ¿Quiere un poco de miel en el té?
examples.trans: Would you like a little honey in your tea?

examples.text: Quedan pocos minutos para el mediodía.
examples.trans: Few minutes remain until noon.

poner.gloss: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)

meanings.en: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)
meanings.note: Irregular: pongo, pon, puse, puesto; ponerse nervioso = get nervous.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas limpias en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two clean cups on the table.

examples.text: Pon la maleta junto al mostrador.
examples.trans: Set the suitcase beside the counter.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.

examples.text: La primera habitación está libre.
examples.trans: The first room is vacant.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.text: Cierra la puerta, por favor.
examples.trans: Close the door, please.

examples.text: Alguien llama a la puerta.
examples.trans: Someone is knocking at the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

quedar.gloss: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

meanings.en: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)
meanings.note: Versatile verb: quedan dos ('two left'), le queda bien ('suits you'), quedar al mediodía ('meet at noon'), quedarse ('stay').

examples.text: Solo quedan dos habitaciones libres.
examples.trans: Only two vacant rooms are left.

examples.text: Esa chaqueta te queda muy bien.
examples.trans: That jacket suits you very well.

meanings.note: In Peninsular Spanish, remover means 'to stir' (paint, soup, or coffee); stem-changing o -> ue.

examples.text: Remueve bien la pintura del fondo antes de empezar.
examples.trans: Stir the paint up from the bottom thoroughly before starting.

examples.text: Rocío remueve despacio las lentejas con cuchara de palo.
examples.trans: Rocio stirs the lentils slowly with a wooden spoon.

meanings.note: Used both as adjective and adverb (corre rápido).

examples.text: El tren es muy rápido.
examples.trans: The train is very fast.

examples.text: Hablas muy rápido, más despacio, por favor.
examples.trans: You speak very fast; more slowly, please.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

secar.gloss: to dry; to wipe dry (secarse = to dry out)

meanings.en: to dry; to wipe dry (secarse = to dry out)
meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> qu before -e (sequé, seque).

examples.text: Seca bien las bisagras antes de dar la pintura.
examples.trans: Dry the hinges thoroughly before applying paint.

examples.text: Con este sol la ropa tendida se seca enseguida.
examples.trans: In this sunshine the hanging laundry dries right away.

meanings.note: Toallas secas = dry towels.

examples.text: La ropa ya está seca.
examples.trans: The clothes are already dry.

examples.text: Prefiero el vino seco.
examples.trans: I prefer dry wine.

seguir.gloss: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)

meanings.en: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: sigo, sigue, siguió); seguir + gerund = keep doing.

examples.text: Sigue todo recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the bridge.

examples.text: ¿El agua sigue caliente?
examples.trans: Is the water still hot?

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.text: Es una pieza segunda.
examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Unaccented conjunction, distinct from accented sí ('yes').

examples.text: Avísame si necesitas otra manta.
examples.trans: Let me know if you need another blanket.

examples.text: Mira si queda leche en la nevera.
examples.trans: Check whether any milk is left in the fridge.

meanings.note: Followed by bare nouns (sin azúcar, sin sal) or infinitives (sin abrir = unopened).

examples.text: Tomo el té sin azúcar, gracias.
examples.trans: I take my tea without sugar, thank you.

examples.text: Salió de casa sin abrigo.
examples.trans: He left home without a coat.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave, señora.
examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Por la tarde = in the afternoon; ¡Buenas tardes! = Good afternoon!; llegar tarde = arrive late.

examples.text: ¡Buenas tardes! ¿Tienen una habitación libre?
examples.trans: Good afternoon! Do you have a room free?

examples.text: Perdón por llegar un poco tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving a little late.

meanings.note: Pleasantly warm (not scalding hot).

examples.text: Es una pieza templada.
examples.trans: It is a warm piece.

examples.text: Toque el radiador: arriba está templado, pero abajo se está enfriando.
examples.trans: Touch the radiator: the top is lukewarm, yet the bottom is getting cold.

meanings.note: Shade tree with heart-shaped green leaves; its blossom makes tila tea.

examples.text: Las hojas de tilo tienen un tono verde precioso.
examples.trans: Linden leaves have a gorgeous shade of green.

examples.text: En la plaza vieja dan sombra cuatro tilos altos.
examples.trans: Four tall linden trees shade the old square.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

venir.gloss: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)

meanings.en: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)
meanings.note: Irregular: vengo, vienes, viene, vine.

examples.text: Gracias por venir esta mañana.
examples.trans: Thank you for coming this morning.

examples.text: Nos vemos la semana que viene.
examples.trans: See you next week.

meanings.note: Plural los ventiladores.

examples.text: Pon el ventilador a velocidad suave en el pasillo.
examples.trans: Set the fan to low speed in the hallway.

examples.text: Dos ventiladores mueven el aire seco hacia las ventanas.
examples.trans: Two fans move dry air toward the windows.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Me gusta el té verde.
examples.trans: I like green tea.

examples.text: Las contraventanas son verdes.
examples.trans: The shutters are green.

meanings.note: Natural grain lines in timber or stone (seguir la veta).

examples.text: Lija siempre la tabla siguiendo la veta natural.
examples.trans: Always sand the board following the natural wood grain.

examples.text: El aceite limpio resalta las vetas oscuras del nogal.
examples.trans: Clean oil brings out the dark grain of the walnut.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: El vecino vigila que la caldera funcione bien.
examples.trans: El vecino watches to make sure the boiler runs properly.

examples.text: Vigilamos la maleta hasta el mediodía.
examples.trans: We guarded the suitcase until noon.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.
